items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: Fixed model indices and rate scales: a dimension \(d\ge1\), smoothness \(\beta>1\) with degree \(m=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), class constants \(B,L>0\), \(C\ge1\), a lower covariate-density bound \(0<c_f\le1\), a compact adaptation range \(\Gamma=[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\subset(1,\infty)\) containing the overlap exponent \(\gamma\), a sample size \(n\), an evaluation point \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), the effective dimension \(D_\gamma=d\gamma/(\gamma-1)\), the oracle mesh \(h_{\gamma,n}=n^{-1/(2\beta+D_\gamma)}\) and the risk scale \(r_{\gamma,n}=h_{\gamma,n}^\beta\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: An observational causal model on the covariate cube \(\mathcal X=[0,1]^d\): a probability law on \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\in\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^3\) whose observed marginal \(P\) is the law of \(Z=(X,A,Y)\), with covariate density \(f\), propensity \(e(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)\), treated response curve \(\mu_1(x)=\mathbb E[Y(1)\mid X=x]\) taken as its continuous Hölder representative, treated-covariate density \(g_1=ef/P(A=1)\), the Hölder ball \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\), the law class \(\mathcal P_\gamma\), population treated microcell masses \(q_{Q\ell}\), their cell minima \(q_Q\) and order statistics \(q_{(k)}\), Dorn's local anti-concentration property, the thin-strip law and the bounded Bernoulli testing pair.

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: Independent and identically distributed sampling: the observed sample \(\mathcal D_n=(Z_i)_{i=1}^n\) has law \(P^{\otimes n}\); all sample statistics (treated microcell counts \(N_{Q\ell}\), the feasible mesh set \(\mathcal F_n\), the selected mesh \(\widehat h\), equal-cell Gram matrices \(\widehat G_Q\), coefficients \(\widehat c_Q\), the estimator \(\widehat\mu_n\)) are measurable functions of \(\mathcal D_n\), and the minimax risks \(R_{\mathrm{pt}}, R_\infty\) take the infimum over \(\mathcal D_n\)-measurable estimators.

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The deterministic equal-cell template and dyadic partitions: the monomial index set \(\mathcal I_m\) of size \(p\), the monomial vector \(U(z)=(z^\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathcal I_m}\), the \(J=(m+1)^d\) tensor nodes \(v_\ell\), the template Gram matrix \(G_0\) with least eigenvalue \(\lambda_0\), the Lipschitz constant \(L_U\) of \(z\mapsto U(z)U(z)^\top\), the microcell width \(\eta\), reference microcubes \(V_\ell\), the candidate dyadic meshes \(\mathcal H_n\), the half-open dyadic partitions \(\mathcal Q_h\) with lower-left corners \(a_Q\), and the scaled microcells \(E_{Q\ell}=a_Q+hV_\ell\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal H^\beta(L):=\{g:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R: g\in C^m(\mathcal X),\ \max_{|\alpha|\le m}\|D^\alpha g\|_\infty\le L,\ \max_{|\alpha|=m}\sup_{x\ne x'}|D^\alpha g(x)-D^\alpha g(x')|/\|x-x'\|_\infty^{\beta-m}\le L\}\). At integer \(\beta\), this uses Lipschitz derivatives of order \(\beta-1\). Here \(C^m(\mathcal X)\) is intrinsic to the closed cube: the classical coordinate partial derivatives through order \(m\) on its interior admit unique continuous traces on \(\mathcal X\), and every displayed derivative, supremum and difference quotient uses those traces. No particular extension outside \(\mathcal X\) is required. Taylor expansions between cube points use the intrinsic traces along segments in the convex cube.

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl:
\[
\mathcal P_\gamma:=\left\{P:\begin{array}{l}
c_f\le f,\quad Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0),\quad
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X,\\[2pt]
P\{e(X)\le t\}\le Ct^{\gamma-1}\quad\text{for every }t\in[0,1],\\[2pt]
\displaystyle
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\sim P_X}
\left(
 \left|\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\right|
 \vee
 \sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}}
 \frac{\sqrt{2\log \mathbb E_P\!\left[
   \exp\!\left\{\lambda\bigl(Y-\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=1,X]\bigr)\right\}
   \mid A=1,X=x\right]}}{|\lambda|}
\right)\le B,\\[8pt]
\mu_1\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
The covariate-density condition is the displayed lower bound \(f\ge c_f>0\); the class imposes no upper density bound.

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: Form \(U\), the tensor nodes \(v_\ell\), \(G_0=J^{-1}\sum_\ell U(v_\ell)U(v_\ell)^\top\), \(\lambda_0=\lambda_{\min}(G_0)\), and the disjoint microcubes \(V_\ell=v_\ell+[-\eta/2,\eta/2]^d\) with \(\eta=\min\{1/(2(m+2)),\lambda_0/(1+L_U)\}\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: For every \(h\in\mathcal H_n\), form \(\mathcal Q_h\), \(E_{Q\ell}=a_Q+hV_\ell\), and \(N_{Q\ell}\). Declare \(h\) feasible when \(\min_{Q,\ell}N_{Q\ell}\ge h^{-2\beta}\), and take the numerically smallest feasible mesh \(\widehat h\), with \(\widehat h=0\) if none is feasible.

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: If \(\widehat h=0\), set \(\widehat\mu_n(x)=0\). Otherwise, at \(h=\widehat h\), compute \(\widehat G_Q\) and \(\widehat c_Q\) for every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_h\), and set \(\widehat\mu_n(x):=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}\{U((x-a_Q)/h)^\top\widehat c_Q\}\) for the unique half-open cube \(Q\) containing \(x\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: Let \(\mathfrak P\) be a nonempty family of probability laws on a common covariate cube \(\mathcal S\), and, for every \(P\in\mathfrak P\), fix a pointwise-defined measurable version \(e_P:\mathcal S\to[0,1]\) of \(P(A=1\mid X=\cdot)\) satisfying \(e_P(X)\in(0,1)\) \(P\)-almost surely. The family-level condition \(\mathsf A_{3}^{\mathrm{Dorn}}(\mathfrak P,(e_P)_{P\in\mathfrak P})\) holds if there exist constants \(\rho,\nu>0\) and \(h_0>0\), common to the family, such that, for every \(P\in\mathfrak P\), every \(x_0\in\mathcal S\), and every \(0<h\le h_0\), \(P_P(e_P(X)\ge\rho\sup_{x\in\mathcal S:\,\|x-x_0\|_2\le h}e_P(x)\mid\|X-x_0\|_2\le h)>\nu\). Here \(\mathcal S=[-1,1]^d\) in Dorn's source and \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\) after the affine transport used in this note. The supremum is the pointwise supremum of the selected version. Consequently the condition is a property of the pair consisting of the family and its selected propensity versions; it need not be invariant under changing a version on a \(P_X\)-null set. The notation \(\mathsf A_{3}^{\mathrm{Dorn}}(P)\), when used for one displayed law and propensity, abbreviates the singleton family equipped with that displayed selected version.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: For \(d\ge2\), let \(X\) be uniform on \(\mathcal X\), put \(x^\circ=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)\), \(R(x)=\|x-x^\circ\|_\infty\), and let \(F_R\) be the continuous distribution function of \(R(X)\). Choose \(1<a<1+d/(\gamma-1)\), set \(S:=\{x:|x_2-x_2^\circ|\le|x_1-x_1^\circ|^a\}\), and define \(e_\star(x):=\min\{1,F_R(R(x))^{1/(\gamma-1)}+\tfrac14\mathbf 1_S(x)\}\). Given \(X\), draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_\star(X))\), take \(p_0:=\min\{1/4,L/(4B)\}\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independently as \(B\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\). The resulting observed-data law is \(P_{\mathrm{strip}}\).

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: This is a descriptive, nonassertive adaptation proposal, not a definition of an estimator or a risk theorem. The proposed architecture would use sample splitting to compare equal-cell fits across polynomial degrees and treatment-count-feasible meshes: the count selector would control the overlap axis, while held-out Lepski inequalities would control the smoothness axis. Its target is a single response estimator equipped with an adaptive-risk envelope over compact rectangles of \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\). No sample split, degree-and-mesh comparison rule, Lepski threshold, estimator, or envelope functional is defined here, and no estimator-existence or risk-bound claim is asserted.

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl: Let \(X\) be uniform on \(\mathcal X\), set \(R(x):=\|x-x_0\|_\infty\), let \(F_R\) be the continuous distribution function of \(R(X)\), and take \(e_0(x):=F_R(R(x))^{1/(\gamma-1)}\). Fix the smooth product bump \(\psi(z):=\prod_{i=1}^d \mathbf 1\{|z_i|<1\}\exp\{1-(1-z_i^2)^{-1}\}\), with each factor defined as zero when \(|z_i|\ge1\). For any constants \(a,c>0\), put \(h:=ch_{\gamma,n}\), \(p_{0,h}(x):=\theta_0\), \(p_{1,h}(x):=\theta_0+ah^\beta\psi((x-x_0)/h)\), and \(\theta_0:=\min\{1/4,L/(4B)\}\). The Lean definition is the totalized measure-valued family obtained by using positive-part Bernoulli weights at these real parameters, taking the common control parameter \(p_{0,h}=\theta_0\), and imposing \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\). Its intended probability-law domain consists exactly of those \(a,c\) for which \(0\le e_0(x),p_{0,h}(x),p_{1,h}(x)\le1\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\); there it is the pair obtained by drawing \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_0(X))\), \(Y(1)\mid X\sim B\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{j,h}(X))\), and \(Y(0)\mid X\sim B\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\theta_0)\). Define \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pair}}:=\{(P_{0,h},P_{1,h}):n\ge1\}\) on this admissible domain; \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}lower\mbox{-}pair}\) existentially chooses fixed positive \(a,c\) in the domain, uniformly for all \(n\ge1\).

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl: Over compact rectangles contained in \((1,\infty)^2\) for \((\beta,\gamma)\), can the two-axis handle in \(\mathrm{def:joint-adaptation-handle}\) produce one estimator whose pointwise and expected supremum risks attain the oracle scale for every pair, and what logarithmic penalty, if any, is minimax unavoidable?

items.label: Assumption A-8
Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_\gamma\), \(\mu_1(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\), and the Holder representative fixes the target at every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For every measurable \(E\subseteq\mathcal X\) with \(P(X\in E)=u\), \(P(A=1,X\in E)\ge ((\gamma-1)/\gamma)C^{-1/(\gamma-1)}u^{\gamma/(\gamma-1)}\). Consequently, at every dyadic mesh \(h\), the ordered weakest-cell masses satisfy \(q_{(k)}\ge\kappa_\Gamma h^{D_\gamma}k^{1/(\gamma-1)}\) for all \(1\le k\le|\mathcal Q_h|\), with one \(\kappa_\Gamma>0\) uniform over \(\gamma\in\Gamma\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl: The tensor nodes are unisolvent for total-degree-\(m\) polynomials, so \(\lambda_0>0\). For every feasible mesh \(h\in\mathcal F_n\) and every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_h\), the threshold \(N_{Q\ell}\ge h^{-2\beta}\) makes every \(N_{Q\ell}\) positive, and the equal-cell matrix satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat G_Q)\ge\lambda_0/2\), independently of the within-microcell distribution of treated observations.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl: For sufficiently small fixed \(a,c>0\), both components \(P_{0,h}\) and \(P_{1,h}\) of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pair}}\), with \(h=ch_{\gamma,n}\), belong to \(\mathcal P_\gamma\), have \(Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,B\}\), satisfy \(\operatorname{KL}(P_{0,h}^{\otimes n},P_{1,h}^{\otimes n})\le 1/8\), and obey \(|\mu_{1,P_{1,h}}(x_0)-\mu_{1,P_{0,h}}(x_0)|\ge c_0r_{\gamma,n}\) for a constant \(c_0>0\).

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl: For every compact \(\Gamma\subset(1,\infty)\), there exist finite positive constants \(K\) and \(K'\), and \(n_0\), such that, for all \(n\ge n_0\), \(\gamma\in\Gamma\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_\gamma\), an event \(\mathcal E_n\) with \(P(\mathcal E_n^c)\le n^{-2}\) satisfies \(0<\widehat h\le Kh_{\gamma,n}\), \(N_{Q\ell}\ge nq_{Q\ell}/5\) at the selected mesh, and, after ordering selected cubes by \(q_Q\), each centered coefficient error is conditionally sub-Gaussian with variance proxy at most \(K\min\{\widehat h^{2\beta},n^{-1}\widehat h^{-D_\gamma}k^{-1/(\gamma-1)}\}\). More generally, if ordered centered variables have variance proxies bounded by \(\min\{a^2,b^2k^{-\alpha}\}\), then \(\mathbb E\max_k|Z_k|\le K_\alpha a\sqrt{1+\log_+((b/a)^{2/\alpha})}\). With \(a=K\widehat h^\beta\), \(b=Kn^{-1/2}\widehat h^{-D_\gamma/2}\), and \(\alpha=1/(\gamma-1)\), this yields \(\mathbb E[\max_{Q}\|\widehat c_Q-\mathbb E(\widehat c_Q\mid(X_i,A_i)_{i=1}^n)\|_\infty\mid(X_i,A_i)_{i=1}^n]\le K\widehat h^\beta\sqrt{1+\log_+(h_{\gamma,n}/\widehat h)}\le K'r_{\gamma,n}\). Thus the series introduces no \(\log n\) factor.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
Dorn's Section 2 fixes an arbitrary nonempty family \(\mathfrak P\), common constants including finite \(\gamma_0>1\), and selected propensity representatives.  Assumptions 1 and 2 impose on every member exactly the positivity, moment, variance, global-tail, uniform-design, Gaussian, and source H\"older-seminorm conditions transcribed in \(\mathrm{lem:dorn\mbox{-}source\mbox{-}rate\mbox{-}transcription}\), and Assumption 3 is the family-level selected-representative condition in \(\mathrm{def:dorn\mbox{-}a3}\).  For each already fixed setup satisfying Assumptions 2 and 3, define
\[
 r^*_{\mu,n}:=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d\gamma_0/(\gamma_0-1))}.
\]
Clause (ii) is the valid source comparator: after the family, its common constants including \(\gamma_0\), and its selected representatives have been fixed, there exists an estimator \(\widehat\mu\) for that setup such that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a finite, setup-dependent \(c(\varepsilon)\) satisfying
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}
 P\!\left\{\|\widehat\mu-\mu_P\|_{L^\infty(P)}
 >c(\varepsilon)r^*_{\mu,n}\right\}\le\varepsilon.
\]
The estimator is pointwise sample-measurable, and for every sample size, family member, and finite threshold the displayed \(L^\infty(P)\) exceedance event is measurable, so the display uses ordinary probability rather than an outer-measure extension.  The estimator witness, the rate through \(\gamma_0\), \(c(\varepsilon)\), and proof constants may depend on the fixed setup; neither a common estimator nor uniform constants over setups are asserted.  This upper rate contains no logarithmic factor.  Clause (i) prints the attribution that there exists \(c>0\) such that
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}
 P\!\left\{|\widehat\mu(0)-\mu_P(0)|>cr^*_{\mu,n}\right\}>0.
\]
The latter display is not a valid logical lower gate under the literal assumptions: those assumptions contain no family-richness or closure requirement, and a singleton family with known regression, or any admissible family sharing a known regression curve, has zero minimax regression error.  Accordingly, clause (i) is retained only as the paper's underqualified printed attribution.

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl: For fixed \(d\ge1\), \(\beta>1\), and \(m=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), there is a finite constant \(K_{d,\beta}\) with the following property.  If \(u\in C^m([-1,1]^d)\), \(\|u\|_\infty\le M_0\), and every derivative of order \(m\) has \((\beta-m)\)-H\"older seminorm at most \(L_0\), then, for \(T(x)=2x-\mathbf1\), the function \(u\circ T\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^\beta(K_{d,\beta}(M_0+L_0))\) on \([0,1]^d\).

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
Let \(r_n>0\) and let \(\mathfrak P\) be a nonempty statistical family for which the target regression curve is the same known function \(\mu^\circ\) under every \(P\in\mathfrak P\).  Then, for every \(c>0\) and every evaluation point \(x_0\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}
 P\{|\widehat\mu(x_0)-\mu_P(x_0)|>cr_n\}=0.
\]
In particular, fix finite \(\gamma>1\), let \(X\) be uniform on \([-1,1]^d\), take \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and take \(Y\mid X,A\sim N(0,1)\).  The singleton containing this law satisfies Dorn's Assumptions 1--3 for suitable common constants and every \(\beta,L_0>0\), but its regression curve is known and its minimax error is zero.  Thus the per-law restrictions do not by themselves imply a positive minimax lower bound when the model family may be an arbitrary nonempty subfamily.

items.label: Lemma lem:global-holder-extension
items.nl: Fix a dimension \(d\ge0\), an integer \(m\ge0\), and an exponent \(0<s\le1\). There is a constant \(K_{\mathrm{ext}}>0\), depending only on \(d\), \(m\), and \(s\), with the following property. Let \(L\ge0\) and let \(g:[-1,1]^d\to\mathbb R\) belong to \(C^m([-1,1]^d)\) in the intrinsic closed-cube sense of \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\), transported to the cube \([-1,1]^d\): the coordinate derivatives \(D^\alpha g\), \(|\alpha|\le m\), exist on the interior and admit continuous traces on \([-1,1]^d\), and, read through those traces, \(\sup_{z\in[-1,1]^d}|D^\alpha g(z)|\le L\) for every \(|\alpha|\le m\) and \(|D^\alpha g(z)-D^\alpha g(z')|\le L\|z-z'\|_\infty^{s}\) for every \(|\alpha|=m\) and all \(z,z'\in[-1,1]^d\). Then there is a function \(g_{\mathrm{ext}}\in C^m(\mathbb R^d)\) such that \(g_{\mathrm{ext}}(z)=g(z)\) for every \(z\in[-1,1]^d\), \(\sup_{z\in\mathbb R^d}\|\mathrm D^{k}g_{\mathrm{ext}}(z)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_{\mathrm{ext}}L\) for every \(0\le k\le m\), and \(\|\mathrm D^{m}g_{\mathrm{ext}}(z)-\mathrm D^{m}g_{\mathrm{ext}}(z')\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_{\mathrm{ext}}L\|z-z'\|_\infty^{s}\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathbb R^d\). Here \(\mathrm D^{k}\) is the Fréchet derivative of order \(k\), with order zero read as the function itself, and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) is the operator norm of a \(k\)-linear form on \(\mathbb R^d\) equipped with \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl:
For every \(d\ge2\) and finite \(\gamma>1\), the law \(P_{\mathrm{strip}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_\gamma\), obeys
\[
P_{\mathrm{strip}}\{e(X)\le t\}\le t^{\gamma-1},\qquad 0\le t\le1,
\]
and its displayed selected propensity \(e_\star\) fails Dorn's anti-concentration constants clause even when propensity one is allowed: there do not exist \(\rho,\nu,h_0>0\) such that, for every \(x_0\in\mathcal X\) and every \(0<h\le h_0\),
\[
P_{\mathrm{strip}}\!\left(e_\star(X)\ge\rho\sup_{x\in\mathcal X:\,\|x-x_0\|_2\le h}e_\star(x)\,\middle|\,\|X-x_0\|_2\le h\right)>\nu.
\]
Consequently the full singleton-family predicate \(\mathsf A_{3}^{\mathrm{Dorn}}(P_{\mathrm{strip}})\) also fails.  Moreover, in shrinking cubes centered at \(x^\circ\), the treated-design second moment in the normalized \(x_2\) direction tends to zero.  Hence \(\mathcal P_\gamma\cap\{P:\mathsf A_{3}^{\mathrm{Dorn}}(P)\}\) is a strict subclass of \(\mathcal P_\gamma\).

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
There is one estimator \(\widehat\mu_n\), given by \(\mathrm{def:estimator}\), that uses \(n,d,\beta,B\) and the data but not \(\gamma,C,c_f\), such that for every compact \(\Gamma\subset(1,\infty)\) there are finite \(K,n_0\) for which
\[
\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\gamma}
\frac{\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\mu_n-\mu_1\|_\infty}{r_{\gamma,n}}
\le K,
\qquad n\ge n_0.
\]
For every fixed finite \(\gamma>1\) and every \(x_0\in\mathcal X\), there are \(0<c_\gamma\le K_\gamma<\infty\) such that
\[
c_\gamma r_{\gamma,n}
\le R_{\mathrm{pt}}(n,\gamma,x_0)
\le R_\infty(n,\gamma)
\le K_\gamma r_{\gamma,n}.
\]
The lower bound holds on a subclass with \(Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,B\}\).  The upper bound requires only the bounded treated conditional mean and uniform conditional sub-Gaussian residual condition in \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}potential\mbox{-}outcomes}\); no local anti-concentration, propensity smoothness, conditional treated-density lower bound, or population Gram assumption is imposed.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
Fix \(d,\beta,q>3,M,\sigma_{\min},C,L_0>0\) and a compact \(\Gamma\subset(1,\infty)\).  For every \(\gamma\in\Gamma\), let \(\mathcal D_\gamma\) be this paper's maximal fixed-constant envelope of all individual laws satisfying the per-law restrictions in Dorn's Assumptions 1 and 2 with tail exponent \(\gamma\), without Assumption 3.  Every Dorn source family having these constants is a subset of \(\mathcal D_\gamma\).  Under \(T(x)=2x-\mathbf1\), select
\[
 B_*:=\max\{M,\sigma_{\min}\},\qquad
 L_*:=\sup_{u\in\Sigma^{\mathrm D}(\beta,L_0),\ \|u\|_\infty\le M}
 \|u\circ T\|_{\mathcal H^\beta}<\infty,
\]
where \(L_*\le C_{d,\beta}(M+L_0)\).  Every law in \(\mathcal D_\gamma\) has a consistency-and-exchangeability causal completion in \(\mathcal P_\gamma\) with common \(B=B_*\), \(L=L_*\), \(c_f=1\), and the same \(C\).  One transformed equal-cell estimator, using \(B_*\) but neither \(\gamma\) nor the propensity, satisfies
\[
 \sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\sup_{P\in\mathcal D_\gamma}
 \frac{\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\mu_n-\mu_P\|_\infty}
 {n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d\gamma/(\gamma-1))}}\le K,
 \qquad n\ge n_0.
\]
Consequently the same expected spatial-supremum upper bound holds for every Dorn source family with the displayed constants, without Assumption 3, and it strengthens the valid uniform-in-probability upper comparator in clause (ii) of Dorn's Theorem 1.

If \(d\ge2\), then for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma\) there are finite, \(\gamma\)-specific admissible constants and a Gaussian uniform-design law satisfying the per-law restrictions in Assumptions 1 and 2 whose singleton family fails Assumption 3 for the displayed selected propensity representative.  These witnesses need not belong to the fixed-constant envelope used in the preceding uniform bound.  No Gaussian same-family converse is inferred from Dorn's printed clause (i): without a family-richness condition that formula is obstructed by \(\mathrm{lem:arbitrary\mbox{-}family\mbox{-}lower\mbox{-}obstruction}\).  The matching bounded-Bernoulli converse remains solely the converse for the larger common class \(\mathcal P_\gamma\).

items.label: Cited result lem:gaiffas-degenerate-design-rate
items.nl:
For every \(p>0\), \(\sigma>0\), \(s>0\), and \(b>-1\), consider the
univariate Gaussian random-design regression experiment in which
\((X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed, \(X_i\)
has density \(\mu\), and \(Y_i=f(X_i)+\xi_i\), where the \(\xi_i\) are
independent centered Gaussian variables of variance \(\sigma^2\) and are
independent of the design. Suppose that Gaïffas's Assumption M holds at an
evaluation point \(x_\circ\): on a neighborhood \(W\) of \(x_\circ\),
\(\mu(x)=\nu(|x-x_\circ|)\), where \(\nu\) is regularly varying at zero
with index \(b\). Here and below, a function \(g\) is regularly varying at
zero with index \(r\) when \(g\) is continuous on \((0,\infty)\),
\(g(h)>0\) for every \(h>0\), and
\[
 \lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{g(yh)}{g(h)}=y^r
 \quad\text{for every }y>0.
\]
Let \(\omega\) be regularly varying at zero with index \(s\) in this same
sense, and let \(h_n\) be the smallest positive solution of
\[
 \omega(h)=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{2n\int_0^h\nu(t)\,dt}},
\]
let \((\alpha_n)\) be a sequence of positive numbers with \(\alpha_n\to\infty\) and \(\alpha_n=O(n^\kappa)\) for some \(\kappa>0\), and put
\[
 \Sigma_n=\mathcal F_{h_n}(x_\circ,\omega)
 \cap\{f:\|f\|_\infty\le\alpha_n\},
\]
where \(f\in\mathcal F_\delta(x_\circ,\omega)\) means that, for every
\(0<h\le\delta\), a polynomial of degree at most \(\lfloor s\rfloor\)
approximates \(f\) on \(\{|x-x_\circ|\le h\}\) with supremum error at most
\(\omega(h)\). For
\[
 \mathcal R_n(\Sigma_n,\mu)
 :=\left(\inf_{T_n}\sup_{f\in\Sigma_n}
 \mathbb E_{f,\mu}^{\,n}|T_n(x_\circ)-f(x_\circ)|^p\right)^{1/p},
\]
Gaïffas's Theorem 1 states
\[
 \mathcal R_n(\Sigma_n,\mu)\asymp
 \sigma^{2s/(1+2s+b)}n^{-s/(1+2s+b)}
 \ell_{\omega,\nu}(n^{-1}),
\]
as \(n\to\infty\), where \(\ell_{\omega,\nu}\) is regularly varying at
zero with index zero in the same sense: it is continuous and strictly positive
on \((0,\infty)\), and
\(\ell_{\omega,\nu}(yu)/\ell_{\omega,\nu}(u)\to1\) as \(u\downarrow0\) for
every \(y>0\). The comparison constants may depend on \(s,b,p\) but not on
\(\sigma\); equivalently, the minimax rate is of order \(\omega(h_n)\).

items.label: Cited result lem:dorn-remaining-class
items.nl:
Dorn's Section 2 starts with an arbitrary nonempty family \(\mathfrak P\) of laws rather than defining \(\mathfrak P\) to be the maximal collection satisfying his restrictions.  The selected propensity lies in \((0,1)\) almost surely under every member.  Assumption 1 requires common constants \(q>3\), \(M>0\), \(\sigma_{\min}>0\), \(C>0\), and finite \(\gamma>1\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathfrak P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(|Y|^q\mid X,A=1)\le M^q,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(\mu_P(X))\le M,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X,A)\ge\sigma_{\min}^2,
\]
and \(P\{e_P(X)\le t\}\le Ct^{\gamma-1}\) for every \(t\in[0,1]\).  Assumption 2 retains this family-level Assumption 1 and requires every \(P\in\mathfrak P\) to have \(X\) uniform on \([-1,1]^d\) and \(Y\mid X,A\) Gaussian with common variance \(\sigma_{\min}^2\) and treated and control means in Dorn's class \(\Sigma^{\mathrm D}(\beta,L_0)\), with common \(\beta,L_0>0\).  That class bounds the \((\beta-m)\)-H\"older seminorm of derivatives of order \(m=\max\{k\in\mathbb Z:k<\beta\}\), but its definition alone does not bound the function or its lower derivatives.  After Assumption 3 is deleted, these are the remaining per-law restrictions and common constants; the source still permits any nonempty subfamily satisfying them.

items.label: Cited result lem:dorn-source-rate-transcription
items.nl:
Dorn's Section 2 first fixes an arbitrary nonempty family \(\mathfrak P\) of laws, common class constants, and selected pointwise propensity representatives.  For every \(P\in\mathfrak P\), the selected representative \(e_P\) satisfies \(e_P(X)=P(A=1\mid X)\in(0,1)\) almost surely; write \(\mu_P(x):=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x,A=1]\).  Assumption 1 requires constants \(q>3\), \(M>0\), \(\sigma_{\min}>0\), \(C>0\), and finite \(\gamma_0>1\), common to the fixed family, such that, for every \(P\in\mathfrak P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(|Y|^q\mid X,A=1)\le M^q,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(\mu_P(X))\le M,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X,A)\ge\sigma_{\min}^2,
\]
and \(P\{e_P(X)\le t\}\le Ct^{\gamma_0-1}\) for every \(t\in[0,1]\).  Assumption 2 retains Assumption 1 and requires, for every member of the fixed family, that \(X\) be uniform on \([-1,1]^d\), that \(Y\mid X,A\) be Gaussian with common variance \(\sigma_{\min}^2\), and that the treated and control means belong to \(\Sigma^{\mathrm D}(\beta,L_0)\), for common \(\beta,L_0>0\).  Dorn defines \(\Sigma^{\mathrm D}(\beta,L_0)\) by a H\"older-seminorm bound \(L_0\) on derivatives of order \(m=\max\{k\in\mathbb Z:k<\beta\}\); that definition alone bounds neither the function nor its lower derivatives.  Assumption 3 is the family-level, common-constant, selected-representative condition in \(\mathrm{def:dorn\mbox{-}a3}\).

For each already fixed setup consisting of such a family, its common parameter tuple including \(\gamma_0\), and its selected propensity representatives satisfying Assumptions 2 and 3, Dorn defines \(\beta^*:=\beta(1-1/\gamma_0)\) and
\[
 r^*_{\mu,n}
 :=n^{-\beta^*/(2\beta^*+d)}
 =n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d\gamma_0/(\gamma_0-1))}.
\]
Clause (ii) of Theorem 1 asserts that there exists an estimator \(\widehat\mu\) for that fixed setup such that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a finite, setup-dependent constant \(c(\varepsilon)\) for which
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}
 P\!\left\{\|\widehat\mu-\mu_P\|_{L^\infty(P)}
 >c(\varepsilon)r^*_{\mu,n}\right\}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Admissibility here includes pointwise sample measurability of the estimator and measurability, for every sample size, family member, and finite threshold, of the displayed \(L^\infty(P)\) exceedance event, so the display uses the probability of a measurable event rather than an outer-measure extension.  The estimator witness, the rate through \(\gamma_0\), \(c(\varepsilon)\), and proof constants may depend on the fixed setup; the assertion does not place one estimator or one constant outside the setup quantifier.  The displayed upper rate contains no logarithmic factor.  Clause (i) of Theorem 1 separately prints the attribution that there exists \(c>0\) such that
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}
 P\!\left\{|\widehat\mu(0)-\mu_P(0)|>cr^*_{\mu,n}\right\}>0.
\]
This last display is recorded only as the paper's printed lower attribution, not as a verified logical lower bound under the literal arbitrary-family assumptions.
